deviations.what: keysets clear --apply becomes an audited mutating verb (keysets.clear): its deletes run in one store transaction with exactly one audit entry (identity, set, key or whole set, count), and it joins the registry-wide audit test; t3 shipped it unaudited, like variable writes
deviations.reason: a cleared set is destructive and hard to reverse (only a re-seed restores it) and, unlike a variable, leaves no version history of who cleared what; the decider (assess, 0.946 then 0.964 with the effort and trace facts removed) and the operator chose to audit it in this PR

deviations.what: keyset.filter and keyset.add gain an optional items_field setting: items may be a list of loop output objects (one per iteration, e.g. {results: [...]}), and items_field names the field holding each one's items; a None entry is an iteration with no items; filter keeps the shape (objects keep their other fields, None stays None). Without it, keyset.add placed after a for_each loop stored 0 keys silently
deviations.reason: t5's flow test showed a for_each loop's results port carries each iteration's last step output object, not a list of items, and per-port lists carry None for a skipped iteration; c23 assumed lists of lists. No field name is built in: the live newspaper config sets items_field: results on the add before record
